    National Joe Day, celebrated annually on March 27th, is a fun day dedicated to honoring everyone named Joe, Jo, Joey, Joseph, Josephine, Jody, or any variant. It encourages celebrating friends and family with these names, often by sharing a "cup of joe" (coffee), and sometimes involves informally changing your name for the day. 
    Key aspects of National Joe Day:
     
    • Purpose: To recognize and celebrate individuals with the name Joe or its variations, highlighting that all "Joes" are considered above average.
    • Celebration Ideas: Enjoy a cup of coffee with a friend named Joe, send greetings to those named Joseph or Josephine, or even adopt a temporary nickname.
    • Origins: While featured on National Day Calendar, there is no specific historical, national, or official origin associated with this day.
    • Name Variations: Included names are Joe, Jo, Joey, Joseph, Josephine, Joette, Jody, Johanna, Jodie, and Jo Jo. 
    The day is meant to be lighthearted and is sometimes treated as a "second birthday" for anyone named Joe.

    What is National Joe Day?

    AI Overview
    National Joe Day, celebrated annually on March 27th, is an unofficial holiday dedicated to honoring everyone named Joe, Joey, Jo, Josephine, or related variations. It also serves as a fun day for everyone to "be a Joe" for a day, enjoy a "cup of joe" (coffee), and appreciate the "average Joe". 
    Key Details About National Joe Day: 
    • When is it? March 27th.
    • What is National Joey Day? While sometimes used interchangeably, the primary, widely recognized day is National Joe Day on March 27th. Note that National Today indicates April 16th is observed as National Joseph Day
      .
    • Origin & History: While not a federal holiday, it gained traction as an appreciation day for the common man (the "Average Joe") and a way to celebrate those with the name Joe. It's a day often celebrated on social media by asking people to adopt the name for the day.
    • How to Celebrate:
      • Celebrate the Joes: Wish happy holidays to all Joes, Joannas, Jodys, and Josephines in your life.
      • Change Your Name: As per Facebook, it is common to temporarily change your name to Joe, Joe Jo, or Joey.
      • Drink Coffee: Enjoy a "cup of joe".
      • Dress Up: Some celebrate by dressing like "Average Joe" or channeling "Joe Cool" (Snoopy). 
    Meaning Behind the Name "Joe": 
    • Coffee: According to National Day Calendar, the term "cup of joe" for coffee may have originated from "jamoke," a combination of Java and Mocha, popular among sailors.
    • The "Everyman": The name is synonymous with "average Joe" or the working-class person.
    • Origin: The term is sometimes associated with the Scottish word "joe" or "jo," meaning sweetheart.
